sections.title: Euclid: Galaxy cluster detection through the weak lensing effect - algorithm assessment and selection
sections.abstract: A blind comparison of nine weak-lensing cluster-finding algorithms selects four complementary methods whose combination is projected to detect about 2,500 clusters in Euclid Data Release 1.
sections.claimed_result: The combined methods exceed 70% completeness for low-redshift, high-mass clusters in the stated simulation selection.
sections.caveat: Performance is simulation-based and depends on selection and real-survey systematics.

sections.title: Experimental certification of the nonlocal advantages of quantum imaginarity
sections.abstract: Photonic two-qubit experiments observe violations of an imaginarity inequality and compare the resulting resource region with coherence and Bell-nonlocality criteria.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report experimental certification of a nonlocal advantage of quantum imaginarity.
sections.caveat: The conclusions concern tested two-qubit photonic states and witness inequalities.

sections.title: Coherent and ultra-low-power EDSR with a flopping-mode spin qubit in germanium
sections.abstract: A germanium flopping-mode hole-spin qubit combines charge-noise protection with electric control at very low drive power.
sections.claimed_result: The experiment reaches up to 99.76% single-qubit gate fidelity at 5 mT using -52 dBm device power.
sections.caveat: Multi-qubit fidelity, wiring overhead, and long-term operation remain untested here.

sections.title: Microphysical Diversity in Two Very Closely Spaced Magnetic Switchbacks Observed by Parker Solar Probe
sections.abstract: Parker Solar Probe measurements of two nearby magnetic switchbacks show different temperatures, spectra, intermittency, and current-sheet populations.
sections.claimed_result: The authors argue that localized dissipation at small-scale structures is a plausible driver of heating in one event.
sections.caveat: This is a two-event case study and needs population-level confirmation.

sections.title: How Does Distribution Shift Shape Pretraining Gains in Neural PDE Surrogates?
sections.abstract: Pretraining on 254,909 RANS airfoil solutions reduces target-data requirements, but benefits depend on data budget, coverage, and modeled-physics shift.
sections.claimed_result: At 1,000 target samples, pretraining matches scratch accuracy using 3.25 times as many samples for unchanged modeling and 2.58 times as many with added transition modeling.
sections.caveat: Results are tied to selected airfoil families, flow ranges, and RANS models.

sections.title: Blind Quantum Computation with a Small Quantum Server
sections.abstract: A Pauli-based blind-quantum-computation protocol makes server size depend on non-Clifford gate count and proposes a lower-cost entanglement-based dual protocol.
sections.claimed_result: The protocol gives classical-client blind computation without requiring classical simulability and reduces stated resource scaling.
sections.caveat: This is a protocol result, not an experimental demonstration under realistic noise and overheads.
